A1.justification: Both complete, readable PDFs describe LIFT-GS despite the changed title. Their methods, experiments, figures, eight tables, and Appendices A–B can be reliably matched.

before.justification: v1 reports original segmentation and referential-grounding experiments, loss ablations, data-scaling results, and appendix comparisons.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results in Tables 1–8 and the main-text and appendix figures.

M1.justification: The encoder, mask decoder, pseudolabeling pipeline, and losses remain substantively matched. However, v1 Section 3.1 specifies third-degree spherical-harmonic color coefficients, whereas v2 Section 3.1.2 specifies three color channels per Gaussian. The PDFs do not establish whether this reflects an implementation change or a documentation revision.

E1.justification: Both versions use ScanNet/ScanNet200, ScanNet++, Taskonomy, and Aria Synthetic, with ScanRefer, SR3D, and NR3D grounding evaluations. The added qualitative illustration remains within the existing simple and complex language-grounding coverage.

E2.justification: v2 Figure 3 introduces Semantic Gaussians (Guo et al., 2024) as a qualitative comparator illustrating failures with detailed queries. Numerical comparator membership in the benchmark, pretraining, and appendix comparisons remains unchanged.

E3.justification: The reported benchmark metrics, sensor-versus-mesh settings, training budget, fine-tuning schedule, and data-scaling fractions are retained. Newly specified rendering resolution and point counts document existing experiments rather than establish a revised protocol.

E4.justification: v2 adds query-complexity failure cases in Figure 3 and compares pretraining versus fine-tuning data efficiency in Section 4.4 using existing results. The loss, foundation-model, pretraining-data, and appendix analyses are otherwise retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The statistical reporting practice is unchanged.

E6.justification: All eight tables and retained result plots are unchanged, including 25.7% mAP in Table 1. v2 adds qualitative failures in Figure 3 and newly estimates that 30% additional pretraining data gives gains comparable to 15% additional annotated fine-tuning data.

T1.justification: The grounding, cross-entropy, reconstruction, feature-loss, and Hungarian-matching equations are retained apart from ordering and numbering. The expanded task notation restates the existing mask/correspondence formulation; no new theoretical results or proofs appear.

C1.justification: The principal claims about 2D-supervised pretraining, grounding performance, scalability, and approximately doubled fine-tuning data efficiency are retained. v2's introduction additionally claims that multimodal decoding overcomes limitations of independent dual-encoder grounding.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations linking decoder attention to relational grounding and noisy spatial pseudolabels to the need for fine-tuning. Section 4.4 newly interprets existing scaling results as a data-collection cost advantage. Appendix B's substantive limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 newly documents frozen CLIP text embeddings, handling unused proposals with a no-match token, 512×512 mask rendering, and approximately 50,000 input points. Appendix A.1's detailed hyperparameters and the project-access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2 substantially repositions the work around data scarcity, lifting versus learning, dual encoders versus joint attention, and foundation-model distillation. It adds substantive discussion of works including Semantic Gaussians, LangSplat, Locate 3D, and OpenEQA, replacing the earlier survey organization.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, related work, and much of the method exposition are extensively rewritten. v2 adds finer method subsections, swaps the architecture and pseudolabeling sections, revises the experimental narrative, and adds acknowledgments and an impact statement.

P2.justification: v2 redraws the overview in Figure 1, adds the heatmap illustration in Figure 3, and shortens Figure 2's caption. Existing figures and tables are mainly relocated or renumbered, with their substantive displays retained.

improvement.justification: Expanded method explanations, newly disclosed implementation settings, and the revised overview improve clarity and reproducibility while preserving the existing results and appendix limitations. These are useful but limited gains, tempered by the unexplained difference in Gaussian color parameterization.
